context.problemStatement: Show 0.4 plus 0.3 on a number line.
context.solutionStrategy: Use the quantities given in the problem.
context.groundingProse: Start at zero, jump four tenths to 0.4, then three tenths to 0.7. Scale zero to one.
context.seedNotes: Draw both jumps on a scale marked in tenths.

content.altText: Number line from 0 to 1 divided into tenths, showing a jump of 0.4 followed by a jump of 0.3, landing on 0.7.

labels.description: Begin your addition at zero on the number line.
Move forward four tenths to reach 0.4.

annotations.steps: Start at 0, jump 4 tenths right to 0.4, then jump 3 tenths right to 0.7.
annotations.strategy: I notice that combining decimal distances on a number line works just like adding whole numbers.
annotations.misconceptions: Start at the given number. Count the moves after it, not the starting mark.
annotations.connections: This connects decimal addition directly to measurement and length models.
